full_judgment:
Ms. Salma Masud Chowdhurv, J.:- This Rule arising out of an application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure at the instance of the accused petitioner was issued calling, upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to show cause as to why the proceedings of G.R. Case No.1687 of 2002 corresponding to Ramna Police Station Case No.51(6)02 dated 15.6.2002 now pending before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka should not be quashed and /or such other or further order or order passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The prosecution case in short is that one Md. Faruk Miah, Deputy Registrar, Supreme Court of Bangladesh on 15.6.2002 lodged a first information report with the local Police Station alleging that a Miscellaneous Case appeared Court No.13 which was filed by one accused Ibrahim and others as motion and the said motion came up in the daily cause list on 22.5.2002 as item No.131 and subsequently appeared in the cause list on several other dates and the motion was not heard by the Hon'ble Court and thereafter it was found that the order of the Court with the signatures of two Judges were forged in the order of bail in the said motion and on 15.6.2002 Md. Abu Syeed, Abul Kahir and Advocate Md. Nurul Islam Chowdhury came to Court No. 13 for taking information regarding the said motion and on interrogation they could not give any satisfactory reply and a Clerk of the Criminal Miscellaneous Section informed that the said motion was received from peon Md. Jalal, Peon Iqbal, and one Md. Nurul Islam, a Clerk, who also could not give any satisfactory reply and under the above circumstances the Hon'ble Court directed the Court officers to hand over Advocate Md. Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Abul Khair, Abu Sayeed and Clerk Md. Nurul Islam to the Police and hence the present case. 

 3. Being aggrieved by the proceedings of the case, the present petitioner an Advocate of this Court filed an application under section 561 -A of the Code of Criminal procedure before this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. Mr. M. Sayeed Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused petitioner submits that the petitioner is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case. He next submits that the petitioner is a practicing Advocate of this Court and he has been implicated in the present case out of suspicion only and he is not filing Advocate on behalf of accused Ibrahim Miah and two other in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5690 of 2002 and the filling Advocate has not been implicated in the present case. He also submits that the proceedings against the petitioner is in violation of section 195 of the Code of Criminal procedure as because no complaint was filed under section 195 of the Code of Criminal procedure for the alleged forgery of the signatures of the Hon'ble Judges of this Court. The learned Advocate also submits that the petitioner has speech problem for which he could not give prompt reply to the queries put to him and was thus apprehended and handed over to police. The learned Advocate further submits that one pleader cannot be said to be a party to the proceedings and hence the Court is not competent to start proceeding against him under section 476 and enquire into the alleged offence of forgery. In support to his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in A.I.R.(32)1945 Patna page 362. 

 7. It appears that the petitioner is not the filing Advocate of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5690 of 2002 in which it has been alleged that the signatures of two Hon'ble Judges of this Court were forged. Since the present petitioner has no connection with Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.5690 of 2002 as he is not the filing Advocate of the same, we find no justification in prolonging the proceedings against him in the present case. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that further proceedings of the case against the petitioner would be a sheer abuse of the process of the Court and as such, the said proceedings are liable to be quashed for ends of justice. 

 8. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The proceedings of G.R. Case No.1687 of 2002 corresponding to Ramna Police Station Case No. 51(6)02 dated 15.6.2002 now pending before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka are hereby quashed relating to the petitioner.
